Why calculators can show different results

Same question, different assumptions

  • Your schedule matters: results use the hours and paid weeks you enter — a 2,080-hour year (40 × 52) is only the default, not your schedule.
  • Gross, not net: these tools show pay before income tax, Social Security, Medicare, and benefit deductions.
  • Rules vary: overtime eligibility, the regular rate, and state rules are not decided by the calculator — they come from your pay arrangement.
  • Averages, not checks: monthly and semi-monthly figures are annual averages (annual ÷ 12 or ÷ 24), not four weekly checks added together.

Worked example

Biweekly anchor Friday, January 1, 2027, checked on January 10, 2027.

StepMathResult
1. Next paydayJanuary 1 + 14 daysJanuary 15, 2027
2. Step through the yearEvery 14 days from January 127 paydays
3. Group by monthCount paydays in each monthJanuary, July, December have 3

Total: 3 extra-check months in 2027.

Note: The January 1 cycle is a rare 27-payday year; the January 8 cycle has 26 paydays and extra months April and October.

What this calculator does not do

  • Payday cycles only — this tool does not know your employer's holiday calendar; if a payday falls on a bank holiday, your employer may pay early.
  • Semimonthly and monthly schedules never have extra-check months, so this tool covers weekly and biweekly cycles only.
  • The anchor must be a real payday on your cycle; a wrong anchor shifts every date by the same error.

How to calculate it

Paydays step forward from a known payday in 7- or 14-day jumps, grouped by calendar month

Biweekly anchor Friday, January 1, 2027 → next payday January 15, with extra-check months January, July, and December

Know what the result includes

Use the right assumptions

Weekly and biweekly pay run on weekdays, not calendar dates, so some months collect an extra check. This tool steps forward from a payday you know, in 7- or 14-day jumps, and groups the results by month. Months with three biweekly checks (or five weekly checks) are your extra-check months. Semimonthly pay, which lands on fixed dates like the 1st and 15th, always has exactly two checks a month and never has an extra one.

Frequently asked questions

Do semimonthly workers get three-paycheck months?

No. Semimonthly pay lands on fixed calendar dates, so every month has exactly two paydays and the year has 24. Extra-check months only happen on weekly and biweekly cycles.

What if my payday is not on Friday?

The same 7- or 14-day logic applies on any weekday — only the months change. Enter any payday on your cycle and the tool follows it.

What if a payday falls on a holiday?

Employers usually pay early when a payday lands on a bank holiday. This tool shows the regular cycle dates; check with payroll for holiday adjustments.

References

The official sources behind the 2026 figures used across this site's calculators:

  • IRS Publication 15-T — federal income tax withholding methods.
  • IRS 401(k) contribution limits — the 2026 elective deferral limit (Notice 2025-67).
  • Social Security Administration — contribution and benefit base ($184,500 for 2026).
  • U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division — FLSA overtime pay requirements.
  • Bureau of Labor Statistics, Employer Costs for Employee Compensation — benefits' share of total compensation.
